provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 reads `mdximum` where the 1962 reads `maximum` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `digndtus` where the 1962 reads `dignatus` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `ipsfus` where the 1962 reads `ipsius` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `praesi Digitized by Google Fosta Maji ii diis` where the 1962 reads `praesidiis`; the 1862 reads `6mnium h6stium` where the 1962 reads `omnium hostium` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `perp6tua` where the 1962 reads `perpetua` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `lsetemur PerD6minum Die vi S Joannis ante Portam Latinam Platroitus Ps Rotexisti me Deus a` where the 1962 reads `laetemur Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum Qui tecum vivit et regnat in imitate`; 9 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1862 prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum Qui tecum vivit et regnat in imitate`; the 1862 sets 18 point(s) of punctuation in this oration where the 1962 sets 10; the 1922 Mame reads `Oratio EUS` where the 1962 reads `Deus`; the 1922 Mame reads `inhzrére` where the 1962 reads `inhaerere` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1922 Mame reads `héstium` where the 1962 reads `hostium` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); 3 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1922 Mame prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum Qui tecum vivit et regnat in imitate`. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 590 (artifact PDF p. 704), target-body character coverage 0.97, found by a sweep; Benziger 1962 conformed printing, target-body character coverage 0.93. Recorded limitation: The 1962 prints this under 05-05 with the rubric Commune unius aut plurium Summorum Pontificum. Every 1862 reading here rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone; this lane has no page image of the 1862, and the recogniser damages roughly one word in three there, so where the 1862's letterforms differ from the 1962's the difference recorded above is an inference from the layer and not a reading of the leaf. The 1922 Mame is the check on those places, and it is a full public-domain peer rather than mere corroboration. Not checked: the 1962 page image for this oration, the 1570 (its recogniser is too degraded to control a claim), and the 1604 except where named. || REPAIRED by lane repair-2 on 2026-09-03. The stored target had been a text-layer reading carrying recogniser damage; it has been replaced word for word by a reading taken from the 1962 CMAA facsimile page image at 400 dpi (artifact PDF p. 601, printed folio read on the same image). Line-end hyphens are joined, printed stress accents are dropped, and the ae/oe ligatures are expanded to two letters; punctuation, capitalisation and the conclusion are reproduced at the length the page prints them. The verdict, the antecedent locus and the recorded differences are the original lane's and were not revisited. The marginal number 2517 was read on the same 400 dpi image and is added to the locus, which previously carried none.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui, ad conterendos Ecclesiae tuae hostes et ad divinum cultum
reparandum, beatum Pium Pontificem maximum eligere dignatus es: fac nos
ipsius defendi praesidiis et ita tuis inhaerere obsequiis; ut, omnium
hostium superatis insidiis, perpetua pace laetemur. Per Dominum nostrum
Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

translations.text: O God, Who didst vouchsafe to choose blessed Pius Thy chief bishop for the crushing of the enemies of Thy Church and the restoration of divine worship, make us to be defended by his watchful care and so to adhere to Thy service that, all the contrivances of our enemies being overcome, we may rejoice in everlasting peace. Through our Lord.
